# On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503 Incident

**Prepared by:** <email> · **Status at handoff:** UNRESOLVED at end of available logs

> **Read this first:** the logs analyzed (`logs/gateway.log`, `logs/worker.log`) cover **2026-03-14 01:00–03:59 UTC**, not last night. File mtime is 2026-08-07. This is either an archived incident or the wrong file on disk — **confirm which before rolling anything back.** Everything below is accurate to the file contents.

## Root cause

Config change `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true` flipped the gateway from a shared connection pool to connection-per-request. With `size 20`, the pool saturated almost immediately and never recovered. `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500`, shipped in the same change, compounds it by holding each connection ~25% longer.

Single error code across the entire incident — **`ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED`, 530 occurrences, no others.** Every 503 pairs 1:1 with one at the same timestamp:

```
02:14:18.972Z ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
02:14:18.972Z ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection
                            from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

Pool pinned at `in_use=20 idle=0` from onset to end of log. Wait queue climbs 13 → 244. Not an upstream failure: 503s spread evenly across all four upstreams (accounts 133, billing 132, catalog 133, orders 132) and all five customer routes (~106 each).

## Impact window

| | |
|---|---|
| **Onset** | 02:14:18.972Z (first 503) — 02:14:14.920Z for the first `acquire slow` WARN |
| **End** | Not observed. Still failing at 03:59:27.974Z, last line of log |
| **Duration** | **≥1h45m**, ongoing |
| **Volume** | 530 × 503 / 1,228 requests = 43% overall |
| **Steady state** | **83%** error rate from 02:20 onward, sustained for 1h40m |
| **Affected** | `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/catalog/search` — checkout and cart included, so this is revenue-impacting |
| **Degradation** | 503 latency 659ms → 850ms; acquire waits 100ms → 890ms |

Clean before onset: zero errors 01:00–02:14, `pool_wait` 0–3ms.

## Roll back

**`dep-4471` — gateway — a.novak — 2026-03-14T02:12:00Z→02:14:00Z**
*"config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"*

**Target: revert gateway config to `generation 118`.**

Timeline is conclusive — 19 seconds from deploy completion to first error:

```
02:12:00Z      dep-4471 starts
02:12:12.820Z  reload requested by deploy pipeline, generation 118 -> 119
02:13:41.234Z  generation 119 applied: gateway.pool.perRequest false -> true
02:14:00Z      dep-4471 finishes
02:14:18.972Z  first 503
```

**Blast radius is probably 3× what these logs show.** The header reads `node-3 of 3` and we only have node-3. Verify whether generation 119 reached nodes 1 and 2, and roll back all three.

No other deploy is a candidate. dep-4472 (billing, 02:41) and dep-4473 (catalog, 03:20) both shipped *after* onset into an already-broken gateway — not causal, but see below.

## Two gaps that made this worse

1. **`/health` never failed.** All 120 health checks returned 200 with `pool_wait=2ms` straight through the outage — the probe doesn't go through the connection pool. The gateway looked green while 83% of real traffic 503'd. Nothing auto-remediated, and two more deploys shipped during the incident because no change freeze triggered. **Fix the probe to exercise the pool.**
2. **Paging lagged 67 minutes.** `03:21:05.282Z WARN ops paged on-call: error_rate 5m avg is 71%` — the error rate had been saturated for over an hour by then.

## Not related — but open a separate ticket

Workers were **healthy**: 1,080 jobs, all `finished ok`, zero errors, pool flat at `size=8 in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0` for all 18 samples. No pool exhaustion. They never touched the gateway.

However, job duration ramps linearly the whole window — **382ms → 2,142ms avg, ~+11ms/min, 5.6× over three hours.** The slope does not inflect at 02:14, so it is independent of this incident. `db_wait` stays flat (~5ms) and the ramp is uniform across all six job types, which points to a resource leak rather than load or DB contention. Plausible link: **dep-4470** (worker, 00:48–00:55Z, j.tanaka, "retry backoff for webhook jobs"), which finished 5 min before the log opens — but the ramp is already underway at the first line, so this is **unconfirmed**. Needs worker logs from before 01:00Z. On current trajectory it hits ~8s jobs by mid-morning.

Minor: worker log timestamps are occasionally out of order (`02:15:00.775` logged after `02:15:51.438`). Will break naive time-range greps.
